//: Spark Hosting allows 360 MB of transfer a day, so what is NOT uploaded matters.
The video files are the biggest thing here and nothing at runtime touches them -
the dressing sequence and the turnaround were both extracted to still frames, and
the clips are kept only as the source they came from. Leaving them out saves 18 MB.
The caching rules below matter just as much: with them, a returning visitor
//routing: Every route in this app is a hash (#/shop, #/admin), so the server only ever needs
to hand back index.html. The rewrite covers anyone who types or bookmarks a path.

headers.//: Images, frames and vendored libraries never change without a new filename, so they can be cached hard. This is what keeps a second visit nearly free against the daily quota.
Scripts and styles DO change, and a stale one against a fresh index.html is how a site half-updates. Revalidate every time; the 304 costs almost nothing.
The shell must never be cached, or a deploy does not reach anyone still holding the old one.
